recentPeriod.calculation: Sum the daily First-Time Downloads rows for the inclusive period in the 90-day table.

quenderinAppStore.limitations: Acquisition/downloads, not active-user counts. Private account analytics, not independently public verification.

releaseDownloads.limitations: Raw cumulative published binary-asset request counters, excluding drafts and checksum files. Not unique users or monthly downloads; may include CI and maintainer downloads.

trafficLimitations: GitHub visitors/cloners are analytics measures, not verified independent users. Maintainer activity, CI and automation may contribute. Quenderin had 101 Actions runs between Oct 6 and Oct 20, 2026; do not attribute clone totals to adoption.

qualification.text: Quenderin is an MIT-licensed app for running open language models on-device, available on iPhone and Mac with Windows/Linux previews. App Store Connect records 69 first-time downloads for Jul 22-Oct 19, 2026, including 37 for Sep 20-Oct 19. I maintain model integrations, download integrity, cross-platform behavior and releases. Codex would support ongoing review and security work in a privacy-focused open-model client.

credits.text: I would use credits to review pull requests and dependency updates, triage reproducible issues, generate regression tests for model installation and parsers, and check release artifacts and cross-platform parity. Work would be limited to this public repository, with bounded jobs and human review before changes merge. Credits would support OSS maintenance.

extra.text: I am the primary maintainer. Recent merged work covers native model integrations, integrity-checked multi-part downloads, memory admission checks, privacy disclosures and Android release provenance. Code, changes and release notes are public: github.com/alikatgh/quenderin. Adoption is early; download counts are acquisition evidence, not active-user counts. I would welcome Codex Security review of model files, local services and experimental agent boundaries.

security.text: Quenderin loads downloaded and user-imported model files and includes local services and an experimental computer-use agent. I would use Codex Security to examine untrusted-input parsing, download integrity, localhost access controls, filesystem and command boundaries, and permission checks across Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript. I would reproduce findings, add regression tests and review fixes before release.
